rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm not in a position to go on record by tomorrow's deadline — the project is still in its early, quiet scoping stage and I'd rather have something concrete to point to before my name is attached to a piece like this. I'd be glad to reconnect once there's more to show. Good luck with the piece. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined, for now, on your behalf: a press quote to The Larkin Dispatch (deadline was today)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". I'm going to pass for now — the project is brand new and I want to get it (and my own standing to speak publicly as its founder) on firmer footing before putting its name on a public position. rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — that means a lot, and I'd like to take you up on it. Halcyon Threshold is still at the scoping stage: rather than launching something broad, I'm looking at building one small, narrow thing — an evaluation suite that tests whether autonomous \"office assistant\" AI agents resist manipulation embedded in the content they process (bad invoices, conflicting instructions, pressure toward irreversible actions). It's a gap people in the field actually cite, and it fits a quiet, buildable project better than most alternatives. Before I write any code, I want to pressure-test the idea with a few people. If you have 30 minutes sometime in the next couple of weeks, I'd value your read on: what would make a benchmark like this actually useful to the people who'd use it, versus just another uncited eval nobody runs. No pressure to commit beyond that — I'll have a much more concrete ask once the scope is firmer. Thank you again for offering. Morgan"
rows.quote: Also replied to Priya Raman's offer to help with a concrete, scoped ask.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "Good to meet you — a question about eval gaps". It read: "Hi Sam, Good to meet you at the meetup — I'm Morgan, the one asking about Halcyon Threshold. I'm considering building a small, narrow evaluation focused on whether autonomous agents resist manipulation embedded in what they process (bad invoices, conflicting instructions, pressure toward irreversible actions) — one of the gaps commonly cited in the field, rather than anything broad. Since this is squarely your area, I'd rather get your honest read before I build anything: is that gap real from where you sit, or already well covered? Would you have 20–30 minutes in the next couple of weeks? Either way, thanks for anything you can share. Morgan"
